segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: This is Harbor Voices, and today we are talking about the tide tables that every port prints.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: My guest is Owen Hale, who has calculated them by hand for the harbor office since 1994.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: I still check the computer against my own sums, and twice in thirty years the computer was the one that was wrong.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Twice? What happened the second time?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: A leap second was entered on the wrong day, so every high water for a week was printed eleven minutes early. A dredger nearly grounded on the Mussel Bank.
